page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression ranking in the bottom 10%. However, the 24 dedicated physical cores deliver average multi-core performance across several workloads. Multi-threaded benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 decompression, consistently achieve average results. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 982.55 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 90.83 GB/sec.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the older Intel Xeon architecture, this instance offers a cost-effective option for parallelizable workloads that do not require high single-thread performance or massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, Redis database operations, and moderate multi-threaded data processing. It can also handle basic LLM inference for smaller models, though text generation speeds remain modest.
